hook: Every smartphone holds small amounts of copper, gold, cobalt and more than a dozen other metals, all dug out of the ground. To get about one kilogram of copper from a typical modern ore, a mine moves more than a hundred kilograms of rock and leaves most of it as waste piled nearby. What happens to that waste, and to the hole, decides how a mine affects the land and water for decades.

Leaving leaf litter on a forest floor

figure.caption: Surface mining moves the land above the ore; subsurface mining reaches deep ore through shafts and tunnels.

chain.cause: Mining exposes sulfide minerals in rock and waste piles to air and rain
chain.effect: the minerals react to form sulfuric acid

chain.cause: Acid water flows out of the mine and waste piles
chain.effect: the pH of nearby streams falls

chain.cause: Acidic water dissolves metals such as lead, mercury and arsenic from the rock
chain.effect: toxic metals enter streams and groundwater

chain.cause: Low pH and metals reach aquatic life
chain.effect: fish and insects die and the stream can stay polluted for decades

ideas: Ore is rock with enough valuable mineral to mine at a profit. As rich ores run out, lower-grade ore means more rock moved and more waste per kilogram of metal.
Surface mining (strip, open-pit, mountaintop removal) removes the overburden to reach shallow ore: cheaper and safer for miners, but it destroys habitat and leaves huge waste piles.
Subsurface mining uses shafts and tunnels for deep ore: less land disturbed, but more dangerous for miners and the ground above can sink.
Mine waste causes acid mine drainage, metal pollution, sediment and dust. Land reclamation regrades the land, replaces topsoil and replants it.

misconception.wrong: Once a mine closes, its pollution stops.
misconception.right: Waste rock and tailings keep reacting with air and rain for decades or centuries. Acid mine drainage from mines closed long ago still pollutes thousands of kilometers of streams.

summary: Mining extracts ore and coal by surface methods (strip, open-pit, mountaintop removal), which remove overburden over large areas, or by subsurface methods, which are more dangerous for miners. Waste rock and tailings release acid mine drainage and toxic metals; mining also causes erosion, sediment and dust, and clears habitat. Land reclamation restores mined land, and lower-grade ores mean more waste per kilogram of metal.
